input.recap: The feedback email to the first JusPrin 2 users was drafted in the "Just Print V2 rollout plan" session on Nov 16. Claude only made the Gmail draft, and you sent it yourself.

content.text:
The follow-up email was drafted in [Just Print V2 rollout plan](#local_3e38de32-e8df-4f8c-b26d-1a20db4c0aca). Claude didn't send it from that session. It saved the email as a Gmail draft and you sent it yourself.

What happened in that session on Nov 16:

- **Your request (7:53 AM Pacific):** "Now draft an email to the users who have tried JustPrintCloud so far to ask them for feedback and promise 500 extra credits in exchange. put it in my gmail draft folder and use gmail's group send. but don't send."
- **The draft:** Claude pulled from production the people who had sent at least one message through JusPrin Cloud. That came to 33 accounts, not counting yours. It saved the draft in k@obico.io with the subject "How did JusPrin 2 go for you? (500 credits for your answer)" and turned on mail merge, which is what Gmail now calls group send. The email opens "I'm Kenneth, the maker of JusPrin. You're one of the first people to sign in to JusPrin 2 and use its AI…"
- **The sender:** At your request, Claude added "JusPrin Support" (jusprin-support@obico.io) as a send-as address in Gmail and set the draft to send from it.
- **The replies:** About an hour later you said people had already replied. The same session set up a task that ran every two hours to find replies, give each person their 500 credits, and draft a reply for you to send.

The reply handling continued in the sessions titled "JusPrin 2 feedback replies: credits and reply drafts", for example [this one](#local_0f86997e-919e-41dd-964f-2f7ab4680cce). Several side chats branched off the rollout session (their titles start with "btw:"). They contain the same email text because they copied that session's history, but none of them is where it was written.
